newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary farmers to hinder border crossings.
newsitem.headline: Hungary farmers to hinder border crossings.

text.p: A Hungarian farmers' union said on Monday it planned to obstruct traffic at six border crossings on Wednesday.
"At least several hundred cars will take part in the protest," Gyula Kosa, leader of the METESZ union, told Reuters.

Farmers plan to slow down traffic by blocking one lane and will attempt to hinder traffic at frontiers with all neighbouring countries except Croatia by repeatedly crossing the border with their cars.
Kosa said two smaller unions would join the protest.
Farmers have been organising protests for the last month against the Socialist-led government's 1997 income and social security tax increases.

Last Monday they sent an ultimatum to the government threatening to block border crossings and roads to Budapest unless a demand for unconditional tax relief for farmers earning less than 1.5 million forints ($8,500) a year was met.
Interior Minister Gabor Kuncze said police would prevent METESZ from carrying out its threat.

METESZ is one of the smaller but more radical of around 30 farmers' unions which which have so far failed to establish a common stance over land ownership, distribution of subsidies and farming taxation.
